---
title: "R7. The six quality principles"
description: "The six principles the playbook is built on, and why they matter."
---


NHSBSA analysis informs how public money is spent, how services are run, and what the public is
told.

## The principles

Six of them. Five are GovS 010's own, so following them is how NHSBSA meets the standard rather
than something extra on top.[^src-govs-010-section-2] The clause each one answers to is named
beneath it, so you can see which are the standard's and which are NHSBSA's.

<details class="nhsuk-details nhsuk-expander">
<summary class="nhsuk-details__summary"><span class="nhsuk-details__summary-text">Which parts of GovS 010 are a requirement, and which are a recommendation</span></summary>
<div class="nhsuk-details__text">

GovS 010 separates *shall*, a requirement, from *should*, a recommendation. Only three of its
requirements are substantive:

- the principles below, which the standard puts as "those engaged in analysis shall ensure"[^src-govs-010-section-2]
- a senior officer accountable for NHSBSA's analysis activities
- analytical roles and accountabilities defined in the governance and management framework, and assigned to people with appropriate seniority, skills and experience

The count of *shall*, the clauses and the meaning of *should* are in
[what is binding](r9-what-each-standard-asks-for.qmd#what-is-binding).

</div>
</details>


## 1. Analysis answers the right questions

There should be a clear, shared understanding of the questions to be answered, how they meet user
needs, and **how certain the answer needs to be**. Analysis should be for the public good and aligned
to government policy and organisational objectives.

*GovS 010 principle 1 and section 5.2. See [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd),
phase 1.*

## 2. Using the right methods

Analysis uses appropriate inputs and methods to produce high quality results. It should be
repeatable, independent, grounded in reality, objective, with
[uncertainty](r10-uncertainty.qmd) understood and managed, and it should answer the original
question robustly. That is **RIGOUR**, set out in full in
[what each standard asks for](r9-what-each-standard-asks-for.qmd#rigour-in-full).

*GovS 010 principle 2, and the AQuA Book. See [deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd).*

## 3. At the right time

Analysis is provided in time to be useful. **That is never at the expense of quality assurance.**
Where time is genuinely short, the proportionate answer is a narrower question answered properly.

*GovS 010 section 5.5. See [deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd)
and [working to a deadline](r15-scoring-the-assurance-level.qmd#working-to-a-deadline).*

## 4. With the right level of quality assurance

Quality assurance **and continuous improvement** are built into the way analysis is carried out.
Assurance is proportionate to the impact of the results on the decision, and to the risks of how
they will be used. What a review finds goes into the next piece of work.

*GovS 010 principle 4. See [deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) for the level
and [Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd) for the improvement.*

## 5. Following the right standards

Analysis is undertaken in line with legal and ethical obligations, with public service codes of
conduct, and with those of your own profession.

*GovS 010 principle 5. See [which standards apply to you](r8-the-standards-landscape.qmd) for the standards and
[data ethics and personal data](r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd) for the ethics.*

## 6. Presented in the right way

Analysis supports effective decision-making and meets user needs through clearly presented,
impartial, timely and accessible outputs. That includes being clear about context, strengths,
limitations, and **what remains uncertain, stated plainly enough to act on**.

*GovS 010 principle 3. See [Phase 4, delivery, communication and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) and
[uncertainty, assumptions and limitations](r10-uncertainty.qmd).*

**So the right decisions are made.** Good quality analysis can be trusted to support effective
decision-making and meet user needs.

**An analysis with no agreed margin of error has no threshold to be tested against.** Agree it at
scoping, record it in the analytical plan, design against it, and say at the end what is still
uncertain. [Uncertainty, assumptions and limitations](r10-uncertainty.qmd) is how you measure it,
and [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) is where you agree it.

<details class="nhsuk-details">
<summary class="nhsuk-details__summary"><span class="nhsuk-details__summary-text">Why this sits in the principles rather than in a method</span></summary>
<div class="nhsuk-details__text">

Three sources ask for the agreement rather than the measurement. GovS 010 asks for the levels of
quality and certainty required to be agreed and recorded at scoping.[^src-govs-010-section-5-2] At design, the AQuA Book asks analysts to search the planned analysis for sources of
uncertainty large enough to breach "the acceptable margin of error". Somebody has to have said
what that margin is.[^src-aqua-book-section-7-4] And the
[Uncertainty Toolkit for Analysts](https://analystsuncertaintytoolkit.github.io/UncertaintyWeb/)
gives its whole second chapter to jointly agreeing how uncertainty should be used, before the
analysis is designed. **None of the three is about measuring uncertainty.** They are about agreeing
how much of it the decision can carry, while there is still time to design for it.

Techniques for quantifying uncertainty will keep changing. The agreement will not.

</div>
</details>

## What goes wrong when quality is assumed

Poor analytical quality is rarely obvious at the time. Four patterns are common, and each is a
process failure rather than a competence failure.

<details class="nhsuk-details nhsuk-expander">
<summary class="nhsuk-details__summary"><span class="nhsuk-details__summary-text">The four patterns</span></summary>
<div class="nhsuk-details__text">

**A figure is quoted without its caveat.** The figure appears in a paper. The caveat that qualified
it sat in an annex and did not travel. A decision is taken on a number that meant something narrower than
the reader thought.

**A one-off becomes a production run.** Work built quickly for a single question turns out to be useful
and is rerun for months. Nobody re-assesses anything, because no single moment felt like a decision.

**Assurance is done but not recorded.** Somebody checked. Nobody can now say what they checked, when,
or what they found. The work cannot be defended, and a practice area cannot be evidenced as
compliant.

**Effort goes to the wrong place.** Low-risk work is over-engineered because that is the only
standard anyone has articulated, while high-risk work is assured thinly because the deadline was short.

Each is what the practices in this playbook are there to catch.

</div>
</details>

## Where this playbook answers GovS 010

Three things have to be true of every piece of analysis. The quality and certainty required is
agreed and recorded. The checks that deliver it are proportionate to the risk. And somebody is
accountable for the analysis.

[Deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd),
[the checks, by level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/what-your-level-requires.qmd#the-checks-by-level) and
[roles and responsibilities](../06-roles/index.qmd) are where the playbook does each of them.
